summary: Wasco County, OR crow's nest built in 1929 in a 60-foot ponderosa pine; abandoned, with ladder and guy-wire remains on the summit; nearby trails closed after the 2026 Grasshopper Fire.

facts.design: Crow's nest atop a 60-foot ponderosa pine, reached by an access ladder
facts.status_note: Remains only: a section of ladder, guy cables and a few planks from the nest, per Oregon Hikers and a November 2021 visit

access.note: Oregon Hikers' page for the Rocky Butte to Grasshopper Point hike carries a July 2026 notice that the trails are closed due to activity from the Grasshopper Fire

visit.trail_note: Oregon Hikers says the route past the site is for experienced hikers only. The closure notice is dated July 2026, so check the current Forest Service closure before going.

corrections.why: Remains are on the summit (ladder remnants and guy cables). The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the site as Abandoned, not gone.

corrections.proposed: Remove from Rocky Butte. The 1969 removal belongs to Grasshopper Point, about 1.5 miles west.
corrections.why: Fire Lookout.com places Rocky Butte 1.5 miles east of Grasshopper Point, which it says was removed in 1969. The removal is of the other tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief recorded Fire Lookout.com as standing. That page says only that the crow's nest has been abandoned for many years, and the association lists the site as Abandoned. The record keeps ruins, because Oregon Hikers and the November 2021 visit describe remnants only. A Roaming Civic Mt Hood tag page says the nest still stands today, which conflicts with those accounts and is not resolved here.
Fire Lookout.com and The Roaming Civic give 4,796 feet; Oregon Hikers gives 4,775 feet. The record keeps 1461.8 m (4,796 ft).
Oregon Hikers dates the Grasshopper Point tower's loss to 1967. Fire Lookout.com and the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register say about 1969. The dates concern that other tower, not Rocky Butte.

notes_for_editor: The 1929 build year agrees across three sources (Fire Lookout.com, Oregon Hikers and The Roaming Civic 2021 article). The Roaming Civic Mt Hood tag page (source 8) was read in full on 2026-10-10. It says there is minimal information on when Rocky Butte was built, that it pre-dates 1930, and that the nest 'still stands today' with most of the ladder present. The story now carries the date caveat but not the standing claim, and the status of ruins conflicts with that claim. A human should compare the 2021 article with the tag page before publishing. The closure notice is dated July 2026 and the Oregon Hikers pages are undated, so re-check the Forest Service closure before publishing the access line. No new photos; the firelookout.com photo is already on the record.
